title: Proper pushforward and exchange compatibility for condensed finite-to-Qbar coefficient extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, write $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and order its finite intermediate extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ by inclusion [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Use the condensed rings $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ on profinite sets and the coefficient pullback $p_T^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Define $\underline\Omega(S)$ to be the subring of $C(S,\Omega)$ consisting of continuous functions whose values lie in one finite intermediate extension, with restrictions by precomposition. Thus $\underline\Omega$ is the archived $\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$, not the full continuous-function sheaf. Put $E_T^c=p_T^*\underline E$ and $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$. Write $\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ for the bounded constructible module-object category of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], and define $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(T)$ by the identical construction with coefficient ring $\Omega_T^c$: a full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Omega_T^c})$, with bounded cohomology, each cohomology sheaf stratified pro-etale locally finitely presented. No derived completeness condition is imposed. Let $T_{E,F}^T=F_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ and $T_{E,\Omega}^T=\Omega_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ denote derived extension of scalars along the coefficient inclusions. Let $k$ be a field of prime positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and let $X,Y,X',Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$ be $k$-morphisms forming a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f$ proper. For $A=E,\Omega$ write $l_{h,A}=Lh_A^*$ and $r_{h,A}=Rh_{A,*}$ for the condensed-module derived operations and $B_A:l_{g,A}r_{f,A}\Rightarrow r_{f',A}l_{g',A}$ for the specified unit-square-counit exchange of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category], using $A_T^c$ as coefficients. For each finite $E$, the canonical derived coefficient-change comparisons restrict to the bounded constructible categories. They give pullback isomorphisms $T_{E,\Omega}^T l_{h,E}\cong l_{h,\Omega}T_{E,\Omega}^U$ for each edge $h:T\to U$, and the canonical pushforward comparison $T_{E,\Omega}^U r_{h,E}\to r_{h,\Omega}T_{E,\Omega}^T$ is an isomorphism on bounded constructible objects for $h=f,f'$. For $K\in\mathcal C_E^c(X)$, define $S_K$ by first using the pullback comparison for $g$ and then $l_{g,\Omega}$ of the pushforward comparison for $f$, and define $U_K$ by first using the pushforward comparison for $f'$ and then $r_{f',\Omega}$ of the pullback comparison for $g'$. Their types are
$$S_K:T_{E,\Omega}^{Y'}l_{g,E}r_{f,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}l_{g,\Omega}r_{f,\Omega}T_{E,\Omega}^{X}K,$$
$$U_K:T_{E,\Omega}^{Y'}r_{f',E}l_{g',E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{f',\Omega}l_{g',\Omega}T_{E,\Omega}^{X}K.$$
They satisfy the equality of specified arrows
$$B_\Omega(T_{E,\Omega}^{X}K)\circ S_K=U_K\circ T_{E,\Omega}^{Y'}(B_E(K)).$$
No invertibility of $B_E$ or $B_\Omega$ is asserted.

proof.text: Fix an algebraic E-basis (b_i)_{i in I} of Ω. On any profinite S a section of underline Ω lies in a finite overfield F containing E. The E-linear coordinate map F ≅ E^[F:E] is a homeomorphism: view it as a Q_ell-linear equivalence and apply the finite-dimensional linear-homeomorphism leaf. The finitely many coordinates of a basis of F involve only finitely many b_i, so the section has a unique finite sum ∑ b_i a_i with continuous a_i:S→E. Conversely such a finite sum takes values in the finite compositum of the fields containing its finitely many b_i. These assignments commute with restrictions. The finite-support presheaf is a sheaf, since a finite jointly surjective cover uses only finitely many supports. Thus underline Ω ≅ ⊕_I underline E as modules. Apply the monoidal left adjoint p_T^* to get Ω_T^c ≅ ⊕_I E_T^c, compatibly for every T and every edge. This is a module identification only, not an identification of rings.

proof.text: After forgetting the Ω-action, T_{E,Ω}^T M is ⊕_I M: the map on the i-th summand is m↦b_i⊗m and its inverse is the coordinate expansion from step 1. Tensor balancing proves the two composites are identities. Sheaf sums are exact (sectionwise module sums followed by exact sheafification), so this extension of scalars is exact and its derived functor is computed termwise. A local finite presentation (E_T^c)^m→(E_T^c)^n→M→0 tensors to the same finite presentation over Ω_T^c; its strata remain the same and cohomology commutes with the exact extension. Consequently T_{E,Ω} preserves bounded constructibility. Restriction of scalars V_T is exact, and preserves injectives: Hom_E(-,V_T J)=Hom_Ω(T_{E,Ω}(-),J) is exact for injective J. It also preserves K-injectives by the same adjunction on complexes, since exact scalar extension takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes.

proof.text: For h:T→U use the common coefficient identifications h^{-1}E_U^c=E_T^c and h^{-1}Ω_U^c=Ω_T^c. The pullback comparison α_h:T_T l_{h,E}→l_{h,Ω}T_U sends a simple tensor b⊗m to the identical tensor after inverse image, with inverse obtained by reversing this identification. This holds termwise because both pullback and scalar extension are exact; the coefficient inverse-image composition comparisons make α coherent with identity and composition of h. Restrictions V commute with pullbacks termwise. They commute with derived pushforwards by computing with a K-injective Ω-resolution, which remains K-injective after V by step 2: V_U r_{h,Ω}=r_{h,E} V_T. On each basis summand the canonical pushforward comparison δ_h:T_U r_{h,E}→r_{h,Ω}T_T is r_{h,E}(j_i), where j_i:K→V_T T_T K sends k to b_i⊗k. To verify this is the specified comparison, its adjunct under l_{h,Ω}⊣r_{h,Ω} is T_T(ε_{h,E})∘α_h^{-1} evaluated on r_{h,E}K; on a simple tensor this sends b_i⊗l_h r_h K to b_i⊗K by ε_h. The adjunction bijection therefore gives exactly r_h(j_i).

proof.text: The morphisms f and f' are proper, the latter by proper base change. Therefore both are quasi-compact and quasi-separated: finite type includes quasi-compactness and their diagonals are closed immersions, hence affine and quasi-compact. The base change of either by an affine pro-etale object is still qcqs. Apply the pro-etale bounded-below coproduct node to the family consisting of copies of K, with its common lower bound. The E_T^c are sheaves of Q-algebras. Under step 1 and the exact conservative restriction V, δ_h is precisely ⊕_I r_{h,E}K→r_{h,E}(⊕_I K), by the summand calculation in step 3, so it is an isomorphism. This applies to h=f and f'. No assertion for arbitrary unbounded families or a general non-qcqs morphism is used.

proof.text: The finite-E condensed realization node gives preservation of C_E^c by each l_h and r_h. Step 2 gives preservation by T_{E,Ω}. The schemes are topologically noetherian: their finite-type structure maps are quasi-compact, and the locally noetherian finite-type node applies over Spec k; a finite affine noetherian cover gives a noetherian underlying space. To check preservation of C_Ω^c, take an arbitrary object L of that category. The object-descent clause of the condensed two-colimit node writes L≅T_{F,Ω}L_F for a finite F and L_F∈C_F^c. Apply step 3 for pullback and, for the proper edges f and f', step 4 for pushforward, with E replaced by F; they identify l_{h,Ω}L and r_{h,Ω}L with scalar extensions of the corresponding finite-F outputs. Those outputs are bounded constructible by realization, and their extensions are bounded constructible by step 2. Thus the comparisons used here restrict to the full bounded constructible subcategories. At K, S_K is l_{g,Ω}(δ_f)∘α_g and U_K is r_{f',Ω}(α_{g'})∘δ_{f'}; all their factors are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Keep the exact restriction/pullback and restriction/pushforward identifications from step 3. They identify V(η_{h,Ω}) and V(ε_{h,Ω}) with η_{h,E} and ε_{h,E} at the underlying objects: in the adjunction Hom bijection the identity of the underlying pullback has adjunct the underlying unit, and the identity of the underlying pushforward has adjunct the underlying counit. The comparison θ for the square is identified as well, since it compares termwise inverse images of the same composite scheme morphism using the coherent coefficient comparisons of the point-pullback node. Substitution in the specified three-factor formula gives V(B_Ω(L))=B_E(V_X L). This checks compatibility of the specified arrows, without presupposing any coefficient-exchange theorem.

proof.text: Use the basis inclusions j_i^X:K→V_X T_X K. After V_{Y'}, the i-th summand of S_K is l_{g,E}r_{f,E}(j_i^X), by α_g and the summand formula for δ_f. The i-th summand of U_K is r_{f',E}l_{g',E}(j_i^X), by δ_{f'} and α_{g'}. Naturality of B_E at j_i^X gives B_E(V_X T_X K)∘l_{g,E}r_{f,E}(j_i^X)=r_{f',E}l_{g',E}(j_i^X)∘B_E(K). Step 6 identifies the left exchange factor with V(B_Ω(T_X K)), and termwise scalar extension identifies V(T_{Y'}B_E(K)) with the sum of copies of B_E(K). These are exactly the desired two routes on each summand of their common source ⊕_I l_{g,E}r_{f,E}K. The coproduct universal property makes the routes equal after V, and faithful restriction gives equality before V. Neither B_E nor B_Ω was assumed invertible.
